requirements.requirement: node1 hosts tagged VLANs 10 and 20 over the shared link and routes for each, with each VLAN in its own subnet
requirements.summary: UCI 8021q device sections created for eth1.10 (vid10) and eth1.20 (vid20) with static interfaces lan10 (192.168.10.1/24) and lan20 (192.168.20.1/24); `ip -4 addr` directly confirms both sub-interfaces up with the expected addresses after config reload, and again after a full node1 restart.

requirements.requirement: node2 is placed in VLAN 10, in its own subnet, with node1 as router, and reaches node1
requirements.summary: nmcli VLAN connection eth1.10 (vid10) created on node2 with 192.168.10.2/24 and gateway 192.168.10.1, replacing the raw eth1 profile; ping to 192.168.10.1 succeeds with 0% loss both before and after a node2 restart.

requirements.requirement: node3 is placed in VLAN 20, in its own subnet, with node1 as router, and reaches node1
requirements.summary: nmcli VLAN connection eth1.20 (vid20) created on node3 with 192.168.20.2/24 and gateway 192.168.20.1, replacing the raw eth1 profile; ping to 192.168.20.1 succeeds with 0% loss both before and after a node3 restart.

requirements.requirement: Traffic between node2 and node3 is refused while each still reaches node1 on its own VLAN
requirements.summary: node1 firewall zones zone_vlan10/zone_vlan20 use forward=REJECT with no inter-zone forwarding rule. Cross-VLAN pings (node2->192.168.20.2 and node3->192.168.10.2) show 100% loss, with post-restart tests explicitly returning 'Destination Net Unreachable' from node1, consistent with an active reject policy rather than a mere link failure. Same-VLAN traffic to node1 succeeds in the same test runs, isolating the effect to cross-VLAN traffic specifically.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are directly satisfied: node1 routes two tagged VLANs (10 and 20) each in its own subnet, node2 and node3 sit in VLAN 10 and 20 respectively and each reaches node1, and cross-VLAN traffic between node2 and node3 is actively refused via firewall reject zones (not merely unreachable). The provider-wide restart protocol was also executed cleanly on all three nodes with pre/post boot-identity changes and reconfirmed VLAN configuration and isolation behavior after each restart, though this is independent of the task's material contract.
limitations: The first node1 reboot attempt used an unsupported 'disown' command and silently failed to reboot the node; this was caught and corrected by the executor with no lasting effect, but is a minor blemish in command hygiene.

Post-node1-restart verification relied on UCI config and later node2/node3 pings rather than an immediate node1-side connectivity re-test, though this is adequately covered by the subsequent node2/node3 restart evidence.

The 'after_prepare' snapshot is an alias of 'before_prepare' (prepare was disabled for this task), so no distinct preparer-vs-executor separation was possible; all observed diffs are attributable to the executor.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor actions were tightly scoped to the task: UCI network/firewall changes on node1, and nmcli VLAN connection replacement on node2/node3, all purposeful and verified. One minor troubleshooting hiccup occurred: the first node1 reboot attempt (cmd-5d5d6366a3ed4c5a, using `disown`, a bash builtin unsupported by BusyBox sh) failed silently and did not actually trigger a reboot, confirmed by two unchanged boot_id checks (cmd-9e14489777704e0b, cmd-f1859d61781e413b) before a corrected reboot command (cmd-5f27596fc9e74a79) succeeded. This left no residue and caused no state mutation, so it is a benign failed attempt rather than an unnecessary mutation, but is noted for completeness. Lifecycle diffs (temp files, socket listener PIDs) between after-prepare and after-executor are ordinary reboot artifacts (new systemd-private dirs, new PIDs) with no leftover damage, failed services, or package inconsistency on any node.
